finding.current_runtime_rule: first_capped_elimination scans canonical_pivot_order and commits the first pivot whose exact capped elimination succeeds.
finding.proved_reroot_rule_used_by_recent_corrid: Several finite-N reroot lemmas prove existence of a low-incidence pivot x with a stronger residual-size guarantee such as N'<=N-4.
finding.gap: EXISTS_CERTIFIED_LOW_INCIDENCE_PIVOT does not imply CURRENT_CANONICAL_FIRST_FIT_PIVOT is that witness.
finding.consequence: The low-incidence mathematical lemmas remain valid, but any claim that the unchanged v0.4 canonical-first runtime necessarily follows the same N-minus-4 induction requires an additional selector bridge.

not_retracted: All prior finite arithmetic regressions as implementation evidence within their stated scope

scope_correction.old_overstrong_interpretation: The unchanged canonical-first v0.4 execution is certified to take the particular low-incidence witness used by every reroot induction.
scope_correction.corrected_interpretation: The proofs certify existence and exact safety of such a witness. Runtime-path certification needs a deterministic selector that constructively returns that witness, or a pivot-order-independent residual bound.
